newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on profit-taking, seen higher.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds ended lower after falling back from early gains prompted by a rise in Vnesh debt and client demand, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Prices firmed in the morning on client buying and following Vnesh debt but then eased on profit-taking," National Reserve bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said.
Dealers said selling was mainly seen from abroad after the most actively traded tranches 3 to 6 had met resistance at 82.50, 59.40, 42.50 and 48.00 respectively.
Another dealer said the upward mood was still seen on the market ahead of the forthcoming issue of Russia's Eurobond, expected in the end of November.
But Ivanov-Golitsyn said the rise was likely to be moderate as the Eurobond was already priced in.
